title: They bowed in shame…
paragraphs:
They bowed in shame…
But he stood in power—and still chose mercy.
Wait.

If you had the power to crush the people who broke you…
would you?
Joseph did.
And he didn’t.

That tension right there—
that’s where most of us fail.

Because some wounds don’t just hurt… they humiliate.
They replay in your mind at 2AM.
They whisper, “Get even.”
They scream, “Make them feel what you felt.”

You smile in public.
But inside?
You’re keeping score.

You remember who lied.
Who left.
Who used you.
Who buried your name just to elevate theirs.
And here’s the dangerous part…
You start calling your bitterness “justice.”
But listen carefully.

Joseph had every right to retaliate.
His brothers didn’t just offend him—they erased him.

They threw him into a pit.
Sold him like property.
Faked his death.
Let their father grieve for years.

That’s not a mistake.
That’s evil.
And Joseph didn’t deny it.

Genesis 50:20 —
“As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to bring it about that many people should be kept alive.”
Let that sink in.

He didn’t say, “It wasn’t that bad.”
He didn’t say, “I’m over it.”

He said:
You meant evil.
Clear. Direct. Honest.
But then—he drops something supernatural.
“But God meant it for good.”

Same event.
Two intentions.

Human hands—evil.
God’s hand—redemption.
And that’s where everything shifts.
Because some of you are stuck in the first half of that verse.
“You meant evil…”
Period.
Full stop.

You built your identity around what was done to you.
You rehearse the pain.
You relive the betrayal.
You wear the wound like a badge.
But you never crossed over into the second half.
“But God…”
You stopped before grace entered the sentence.
And that’s why you’re still bleeding from something that happened years ago.
Let me say this gently—but clearly.

Unforgiveness feels powerful…
but it’s actually a prison.

You think you’re holding them accountable—
but you’re the one still chained to the moment.

Joseph wasn’t free when he got promoted.
He was free when he let go.
Free when he saw God in the story.
Free when he stopped needing revenge to feel whole.
But here’s the truth we don’t like:
You can’t talk about Joseph without talking about Jesus.

Because Joseph’s story whispers…
but the cross shouts.

Acts 2:23 says:
“This Jesus… you crucified and killed by the hands of lawless men.”
That’s human evil.

But the same verse says it happened
“according to the definite plan and foreknowledge of God.”
Same pattern.
Evil… and sovereignty.
Sin… and salvation.

Men meant the cross for destruction.
God meant it for redemption.

And through that one moment—
the worst evil in history—
came the greatest good ever given:
Your salvation.
My salvation.
Listen.
You’re not just Joseph in the story.
You’re also the brother.

The one who sinned.
The one who chose self over love.
The one who betrayed God in quiet ways no one else sees.

Romans 3:23 —
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
That includes you.
That includes me.

We don’t just suffer injustice—
we commit it.
And that’s where the Gospel gets real.

Because if God only judged evil…
we’d all be finished.
But He doesn’t stop at justice.
He moves to mercy.

Romans 5:8 —
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

Not after you fixed yourself.
Not after you apologized perfectly.
Not after you became “better.”
While you were still a sinner.
Christ stepped in.

Took your place.
Carried your sin.
Paid your debt.
So now forgiveness isn’t just something you receive—
It’s something you’re called to release.

Ephesians 4:31–32 says:
“Let all bitterness and wrath and anger and clamor and slander be put away from you… be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ forgave you.”
Did you catch that?
As God forgave you.
That’s the standard.

Not “as they deserve.”
Not “when they apologize.”
Not “when it feels fair.”
As Christ forgave you.
That’s heavy.
Because forgiveness is not saying the pain didn’t matter.

It’s saying:
God matters more.
It’s trusting that justice belongs to Him.

Romans 12:19 —
“Beloved, never avenge yourselves, but leave it to the wrath of God…”
You don’t have to carry that weight.
You were never built to.
So here’s the question:

Are you still living in
“You meant evil…”

Or are you ready to step into
“But God meant it for good…”?
Because healing starts there.
Not when they change.
When you surrender.

When you bring your wound—not to revenge, not to distraction—
but to Jesus.
And maybe today, for the first time, you stop rehearsing the hurt…
and start releasing it.
Not because it’s easy.
But because Christ is worthy.
If this hit something deep in you—don’t ignore it.
That’s not emotion.
That’s conviction.
And conviction is an invitation.
Come back to Him.
Lay it down.
Say it honestly:

“Jesus, I’ve been holding on to this pain.
I’ve been playing judge.
I’ve been feeding bitterness.
Forgive me.
Heal me.
Teach me to forgive the way You forgave me.”
He will meet you there.
Every time.
